newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rules in favor of rail freight-haulers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rules in favor of rail freight-haulers.

text.p: U.S. regulators have ruled that freight haulers can set rates for through service even if a shipper wants the right to ship partly by another line to avoid the "bottleneck" posed by the through carrier.
The Surface Transportation Board's action this week was in response to three rate cases brought by electric power utilities, each supplied coal from mine to utility by only one railroad.

In the cases, the railroads wanted to carry the coal over its own lines as far as possible, but the utilities wanted to be able to shift the coal to another railroad for part of the way in hope that competition would produce lower rates.

But the board, successor to the old Interstate Commerce Commission, said that giving shippers that sort of rate and route control would defeat the legal provisions protecting each railroad's right to set reasonable routes and rates.

The cases were brought by Central & South West Corp unit Central Power & Light Co. against Southern Pacific Transportation Co., Pennsylvania Power & Light Co. against Conrail Inc., and Midamerican Energy Co. against Union Pacific Corp..
Union Pacific and Southern have since merged.
